name: Deadpan Caption
use: One or two flat sentences where a specific mundane detail turns bleak or absurd.
visual: Optional ordinary photo or no image at all.

name: Top / Bottom
use: Normal expectation on top, bleak or stupid reality on bottom.
visual: Original scene or generic subject; both text blocks short.

name: Fake UI / Error
use: Describe life, work or failure as an app dialog, update log or system notification.
visual: Generic original UI, not a pixel-perfect copy of a proprietary interface.

name: Official Notice
use: Institutional typography and bureaucratic confidence applied to an absurdly human problem.
visual: Generic state/municipal notice grammar, stamps, boxes, formal hierarchy.

name: Dzida Photo + Caption
use: Ordinary or cursed image with a short title/caption that undersells or bluntly reframes it.
visual: Mundane phone photo, screenshot or original crude scene; low ceremony.

name: Post + Comment Punchline
use: The post sets the scene; a dry comment or correction delivers the stronger joke.
visual: Generic social-post layout or text-only dialogue.

name: Cenzo Mutation
use: Literal visual mutation plus matching name/caption mutation. The crude edit is the main punchline.
visual: Hard cutout, wrong scale, mismatched lighting, compression artifacts, optionally amber/yellow cast when culturally relevant.

name: Cenzopolityk Poster
use: Campaign or official-poster dignity sabotaged by one absurd slogan or literal mutation.
visual: Original campaign/state graphic grammar with clear parody cues.

name: Surreal Topical Card
use: One cursed topical thesis stated with confidence, often joining unrelated domains.
visual: Cheap collage or mundane stock-like scene with deliberately inappropriate editorial framing.

name: One-panel Shitpost
use: One strong stupid premise with an internal rule, minimal context and deliberate anti-polish.
visual: Default font, bad crop, arrow/circle, stretched asset or overcompressed original image.

name: Fake Screenshot
use: A plausible-looking but original interface screenshot whose wording creates the joke.
visual: Generic interface language; avoid exact proprietary UI cloning when unnecessary.

name: Cursed Infographic
use: Arrange unrelated labels as if they form a serious taxonomy, spectrum or institutional diagram.
visual: Cheap infographic grammar, arrows, boxes, unnecessary legend, confident labeling.

name: Demotivator Inversion
use: Formal motivational-poster grammar with a caption that removes hope on second read.
visual: Original centered image, thick border and formal caption hierarchy.
